headline: High: ctx can read/write filesystem and APIs while the paired repo is an unverified prompt resource, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a prompt-engineering content repo with no runtime isolation; B observes Claude Code events and can ingest filesystem-backed context. That creates a plausible bridge where A-authored prompt content can influence B if copied into shared files or hooks. The pathway is not proven, but the interaction is more than manual-only because B has MCP/stdio and filesystem surfaces.
conditions: IF A content is placed into a file or hook that B reads
IF B treats filesystem content as instruction-bearing text
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Disable automatic ingestion of prompt files by B
Add a manual review step before B consumes A-generated text
Use read-only mounts for A artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A outputs and B inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches agent entities, MCP servers, harness records, graph data, and runtime logs, and it can access filesystem and external APIs. A is a docs-only prompt repository, so it is less likely to hold sensitive data, but if shared workspace content is present, B can leak it through its documented API and browser surfaces. The pairwise risk is moderate because the leakage path exists in default B behavior, while A contributes the content source.
conditions: IF A artifacts contain secrets or private prompts
IF B is run in the same workspace and uploads or logs those artifacts
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B
Remove secrets from any shared files
Restrict B API access to least privilege
Rotate any credentials present in shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on B outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: B can install packages, run browsers, and write to the filesystem; A is a repository of prompt-engineering material that may also be edited locally. Even without explicit write permissions on A, the pair can contend over shared files or generated artifacts if co-located. Because B supports multiple instances, concurrent modification risk is plausible, though not proven from A alone.
conditions: IF A and B share a writable directory
IF multiple B instances modify the same files or browser state
mitigations: Use per-agent directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run only one B instance per workspace
Make A artifacts read-only
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: B observes Claude Code events and manages context, so it may treat A-produced prompt material as authoritative if that material is fed into its workflow. A is not a validator, only a prompt resource, which increases the chance that B propagates unverified instructions or facts into downstream actions. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A-generated text is used as input to B
IF B forwards that text into actions without verification
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Add a verification checklist in B
Mark A content as untrusted by default
Log source provenance for every B action
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before execution

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and A is a docs-only repository while B exposes runtime logs and external APIs. The only concrete compliance concern is that B handles audit/runtime logs and graph data, so if A-derived content includes regulated data, it could be retained or transmitted. A is cited for being non-runtime; B is cited for the logging surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A artifacts
IF B retains or transmits those artifacts in logs or APIs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts
Review B logging settings
Limit API destinations for B
Delete any accidental regulated content from workspace
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
